target_customer: Independent and multi-provider clinics, starting with chronic GI conditions, that pay for software and a virtual care team
problem: Patients with chronic conditions get short clinic visits and little support in between, and clinics cannot afford concierge-style follow up for their whole patient population.
business_model: B2B software and virtual care team service sold to clinics, which earn more from ongoing patient care
product_category: Digital health, virtual care team platform for clinics

founders.name: Rithvik Seela
education: Stanford, computer science and economics (left to start Gradia)
founders.background_notes: YC page and Pulse 2.0 interview. Spent months working unpaid in clinics to learn the problem.

founders.name: Andrew Zelaya
education: Stanford, computer science (left to start Gradia)

competitors.name: Harmonize Health
competitors.what: Remote monitoring and care platform for medical groups serving high risk patients

competitors.name: Oshi Health
competitors.funding_then: 23M USD raised, reported October 2021 (seven months after the batch)

technical_complexity.rationale: Patient messaging, care tracking and clinic integration are standard health software. The difficulty is clinical workflow and compliance, not novel technology.

defensibility.rationale: Embedding in a clinic's workflow and care pathways creates some switching cost, but the software layer is copyable and rivals had more capital.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition or copying found by the sources opened.

market_need_then: Pulse 2.0 describes 60 to 70 million Americans with chronic GI conditions needing follow up beyond brief visits. Clinics were being asked to deliver more continuous care.

branding.domain_note: Uses gradia.com. No acquisition note found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Mission-led and plain, about challenging archaic medical conventions

brand_strength.rationale: No press or community on the brand itself found. The name is easily confused with Gradient Health and similar names in search.

outcome_analysis: Gradia is active. It raised a 4.2M dollar seed round in July 2023, two years after the YC batch, led by MaC Venture Capital, and works with several clinics in the Southeastern US. No later round, exit or shutdown was found. The record shows modest capital against better funded virtual care rivals, with the clinic-first integration approach as its stated difference. Too little is public to call it a success or a stall.
notes: Seed round stated by the MaC release, Pulse 2.0 and BusinessWire (dated 2023-07-12 in the URL). CB Insights lists about 4.33M over four rounds, so earlier small rounds may exist and are unverified. A GEO profile describing a metabolic health company does not match and was ignored. Competitors were found in search results and not opened. Oshi source is dated after the batch. Headquarters sources conflict between New York, San Francisco and Orlando.
